name: Sahel insurgency
value: JNIM–IS Sahel clashes; 64,000 fled to Niger
summary: JNIM and IS Sahel battles have spread into Niger and Nigeria; 64,000 fled Nigeria to Niger in 2026; no city has fallen
state: Africa Defense Forum reported on 12 Nov that JNIM and Islamic State Sahel fought a second major battle in north-east Burkina Faso in October that killed hundreds of fighters, with clashes spreading since April into Niger's Tillabéri and Dosso regions and Nigeria's Kebbi state. UNHCR said on 10 Nov that about 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria to Niger in 2026 (Reuters via Internazionale). No fall of a capital or major city and no mass-casualty spread to coastal states was found as of 12 Nov, though reporting is thin.
for_you: UK travellers should check FCDO travel advice, which advises against travel to much of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger. Exposure is mainly humanitarian, with displacement and fuel and food disruption.
rubric_hit: Sustained insurgency (Watch); no capital or major city blockaded or fallen, no mass-casualty spread to coastal states (Alert)

sources.title: Eurasia Review (Africa Defense Forum) — Rival terror groups devastate the Sahel
Internazionale (Reuters) — Violence in northern Nigeria drives tens of thousands into Niger

why: Jihadist groups control growing territory across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, driving displacement and coastal-state spillover.
drivers: JNIM/IS-Sahel offensives, juntas, Russian forces, blockades, coastal-state attacks.

rubric.alert: Blockade or fall of a capital or major city, or mass-casualty attacks spreading to coastal states.
